name: rheon-du
description: Where the space under the current directory goes, one record per directory.
author: takakix2
notes:
Where the space under the current directory goes, as Flux signals: one record per directory with the totals under it (size, disk blocks, files, dirs), sorted by path. The tree is walked in parallel. Sorting by size, the top few or one depth are the next command's job. Takes no path: cd there first. Linux, macOS and Windows.

size is the apparent size (what the files say they hold); disk is the blocks they take, which is what du reports -- sparse and compressed files make them differ. disk is null on Windows. Ignore files and dotfiles hide nothing (target/ and node_modules/ are usually where the space is). Stays on one filesystem unless --cross-filesystems. Hard links count once (not on Windows, where Rust does not give the link count). Symlinks count as themselves and are not followed. A directory that cannot be read is not counted, and it and its parents say partial: true; stderr says how many. --max-depth limits what is shown, not what is counted. --all adds a record per file. --threads N sets the walker threads: more for network mounts, 1 for a spinning disk. The library entry (run_in) never exits the process, so a shell can run it in-process. The short name is fusage: fdu was taken by other du replacements.
